speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your neck swelling in detail: how long has it been present, is it painful, and has it changed in size? Do you have any associated symptoms like fever, difficulty swallowing, or voice changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Neck (presenting as a metastatic cervical lymph node from an occult primary tumor, likely from an unknown site or previous head/neck pathology, given the history of colon cancer and the chronic, painless nature of the swelling).

*Note: While the patient has a history of colon cancer, the presentation of a progressive, painless nape of neck swelling is more characteristic of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma (often from an unknown primary) than metastatic colon cancer, which typically presents in the liver or lungs. The next step is to identify the primary tumor source. I will request imaging to evaluate the neck and chest.*

REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Ultrasound_and_Chest_CT.
